STP

Positioning & marketing mix

STP Marketing Model
Download PDF guide

Interactive audience-strategy prototype

Move from a broad market to a message that matters.

Segment the wider audience into meaningful groups, choose the people you can serve best, then position your offer around a specific need, benefit and reason to believe. STP helps replace one-size-fits-all marketing with focused, useful communication.

!
Segments are hypotheses, not stereotypes. Build them from relevant needs, contexts and behaviours—not vague labels alone. Test whether a group is real, reachable, meaningful and appropriate for your offer before investing in a campaign.

Build the strategy

Add audience segments, assess their priority, and write a positioning statement for the selected target. The canvas updates as you make decisions.

STP strategy flow

Move from a broad market to carefully defined segments, selected targets and a clear positioning statement.

0 Target segments selected
Segment by needs and context Target for fit and opportunity Position with value and proof
Step 1 Segmentation Identify meaningful groups with distinct needs, contexts or behaviours.
→
Step 2 Targeting Prioritise segments based on attractiveness and your ability to serve them well.
→
Step 3 Positioning State how the chosen audience should understand your offer compared with alternatives.

Evidence check

STP review prompts

    This prototype supports marketing planning and workshop facilitation. It does not replace customer research, accessibility research, market sizing, legal compliance or campaign testing. Avoid using sensitive characteristics to unfairly exclude, exploit or discriminate against people; validate segments through ethically gathered evidence.
